title: Subquadratic’s New Snap Model Processes 100K Tokens in Under 1 Second
summary:
Subquadratic has released a long-context decision model called SubQ Snap that can manage 384K tokens of multimodal data, 12x the capacity of its rival, Jev. The new model processes 100K tokens and returns a decision in under one second, costing $0.05 per million input tokens with output provided for free. In testing, Snap scored 61.7 on Decision Index v0.2.1 compared to 57.9 for Jev and outperformed it on 13 of 16 enterprise benchmarks.

Designed for "micro-decisions" such as lead qualification and support ticket routing, Snap keeps compute per token constant as context grows to avoid the latency of general LLMs. The tool is available now, with the first 10,000 users receiving 100M free input tokens. Subquadratic noted that latency may be variable as they tune the platform and add compute to meet demand.

Introducing SubQ Snap, the first long-context decision model for real enterprise work.

Snap is the only decision model or LLM where compute per token stays constant as context grows.

• 384K tokens of multimodal context, 12x larger than Jev.
• 61.7 on Decision Index v0.2.1 vs Jev’s 57.9, outperforming on 13 of 16 enterprise benchmarks.
•Processes 100K tokens and returns a decision in under one second.
•$0.05/MM input tokens. Output is free.

Available today to anyone.

The first 10,000 sign-ups get 100M free input tokens.

We’ll likely hit capacity fast and will add users as we add compute. Compute offers welcome 🙂.

Latency will be variable as we tune the platform to this new model and category of users. 

Model speeds are 80ms for minimal context, 250ms for 32k, 660ms for 100k, and 2.5 seconds for 384k.

Subquadratic says SubQ Snap processes 100K tokens and returns a decision in *under a second*.

Its new decision model supports up to 384K tokens in one call, including text and images. The team’s pricing is $0.05 per million input tokens, cached or uncached, with free output.

Lead qualification is a good example: check each new lead against deals you’ve already won or lost, then let a frontier model write the outreach for the ones that look promising. Your past deals end up guiding the next ones.
